_why: Canonical data for board 373: the CED Essential Knowledge codes standing in
student-visible text on the AP CSA lesson pages, and what each one becomes.
The rule is 'Citing the CED to students' in
docs/ap-cyber-unit1-ced-realignment.md, and it is course-agnostic: the code
is teacher knowledge, so name the idea, not the code.
MEASURED 2026-09-21 against the live pages, through lib/storefront-fetch.js.
178 citations on 19 of the 38 Units 2-4 lesson pages. lib/cyber-ek-density.js
reports 0 of them in a protected placement, and on these pages that is the
true answer rather than a blind spot: none of the four structures it protects
(the id="ekNN-body" coverage table, an evidence sentence inside a faq-item or
info-box, a Answer Key: block, an atk-tag card tag) exists on
any CSA lesson page. Checked by grepping all 38 bodies for each marker: zero
hits. The three pages carrying the word 'teacher' at all are 3.1, 3.3 and 3.4,
and none of those three carries a single EK code.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY LEFT ALONE, AND THE ONE THAT ALMOST WAS BY MISTAKE.
8 of the 178 sit inside a <script> block, and an earlier version of this file
called all 8 search-engine metadata and left all 8. Seven of them are: they
are in <script type="application/ld+json">, in strings like 'Aligned to
2025-2026 CED topic 2.1.A.', which is metadata rather than page text, and
this repo's own definition of a visible citation (visibleCitations in
scripts/cyber-ek-thin-csv.js) excludes script content.
THE EIGHTH IS NOT METADATA. It is in a plain <script> on 3.6 holding the Bug
Hunt game's question data, in the explanation string a student is shown when
they check an answer: 'same-class access allows other.count inside Inventory
(EK 3.6.A.3).' It renders on the page at runtime. Reading the tag rather than
running the check is what hid it: seven of eight carried the ld+json type and
the count looked uniform. It is cut, as a counted prose replacement, because
the mechanical rules deliberately never reach inside a <script>.
So 171 are cut and 7 are not, and the number is stated both ways wherever it
is reported rather than rounded to a nicer one.

prose.why: MCQ 7 feedback, and the one place where dropping the codes leaves nothing: '(primitives) + (objects).' is not a sentence. Answer B is 'Primitives: copy of value; Objects: copy of reference to same object; methods CAN mutate the object', so the replacement says that.
prose.repl: A primitive parameter gets a copy of the value. An object parameter gets a copy of the reference, so the method can change the object it points at.
